newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks firm, seen taking a breather.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks firm, seen taking a breather.

text.p: Austrian shares ended moderately higher on Tuesday, boosted by futures-linked buying after investors turned a blind eye to overnight losses on Wall Street.

The ATX index of 21 key stocks rose 0.42 percent or 5.03 points to close the session at 1,199.17, just below the day's high of 1,199.72. Among its constituents, 13 winners outnumbered seven losers, one issue closed unchanged.

Traders said the market was expected to trudge lower over the short term amid a dearth of fresh buying incentives and was unlikely to break the key 1,200 mark soon. "We're lacking liquidity," said one.
Brick maker Wienerberger Baustoffindustrie rose 7.2 schillings to 2,257 after posting a limp set of final 1996 earnings, which traders said were largely in line with expectations.
Gainers were topped by beverage group BBAG, rising 2.69 percent to 726 schillings.

Outside of the blue-chip ATX index, but included in continuous trading, water treatment company BWT jumped 17 schillings to 1,649 after reporting a record set of 1996 group earnings. The stock has gained as much as 47 percent since the start of the year.

Airport operator decliner Flughafen led the day's decliners, falling 2.87 percent to close at 500 schillings on hefty turnover of almost 82,000 lots. Traders said the share had sailed through several key support levels and continued to look weak from a technical point of view.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index rose 1.18 points to 452.55.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for May delivery firmed 4.5 points to 1,192 on turnover of 15,008 contracts.
